title: Pluggable Routing Contracts Linter and Safe Migration Plan
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Replace the fragile ad-hoc routing config checks with a pluggable 'contracts linter' that validates routing DSL files (region selectors, tier rules, fallback model variants) and emits migration hints for older configs. Background: Current routing rule validation is scattered across runtime code paths and produces inconsistent errors at request time. This causes customer-facing failures during rollouts and makes gradual schema migration brittle. Scope: - Design a declarative schema (YAML/JSON) for route contracts that captures: region affinity predicates, tier prioritization, model-variant fallback graphs, and allowed model families per customer tier. - Implement a linter service that: (a) performs static checks (type/shape, forbidden fields), (b) enforces semantic constraints (no cycles in fallback graphs, explicit region fallbacks), (c) produces machine-friendly migration suggestions and repair patches, and (d) exposes a plugin API so integrations (enterprise constraints, compliance rules) can register extra checks. - Integrate linter into CI (pre-commit hook + server-side validation for Console uploads) and runtime startup checks (fail-fast for fatal contract violations). - Backwards compatibility: provide a compatibility shim that auto-translates common legacy patterns into the new contract model and emits deprecation warnings. Design notes: - Use a typed AST approach so error messages can point to exact rule locations and suggest precise edits. - Linter plugins should be simple Python modules that implement check(rule_ast) -> list of findings. Keep runtime validators lightweight by running only a fast subset at hot path. - Validate region selection by checking region lists, region-set inheritance, and sticky routing predicates. - For tier routing, ensure deterministic tie-breakers and explicit priorities; if missing, linter should flag 'ambiguous-tier-priority'. - Fallback model variants: require explicit compatibility labels on model candidates (e.g., "low_latency", "quantized:q4"), and reject fallback to incompatible variants unless an explicit override is present. Trade-offs considered: - Full runtime schema enforcement would be safest but imposes latency/operational cost on startups and rolling updates. We therefore split checks: deep static linting offline (CI/console) and lightweight runtime assertions. - Plugin system increases complexity but is necessary for enterprise-specific rules. We will gate plugin loading behind feature flags for Private deployments. Acceptance criteria: - Linter implementation in policy-engine repo with unit tests covering 95% of rules. - CI gate added to policy rule PRs preventing merges if linter reports fatal errors. - Console upload integration rejects configs with fatal linter errors, but allows non-fatal warnings with clear UX. - Migration tool can auto-apply simple fixes in 80% of sampled legacy configs. - Performance: runtime start-time validation added must not increase cold-start wall time by >5%. Monitoring & Observability: - Linter errors surfaced in Console with error codes and links to repair suggestions. - Track metrics: lint_errors_total (by code/severity), migration_autofix_rate, runtime_validation_failures. Rollout plan: 1) Merge linter behind feature flag. 2) Run in 'report-only' in CI for 2 cycles to gather warnings. 3) Enable server-side reject on new uploads. 4) Enable startup runtime fast checks. 5) Gradually tighten to reject known problematic patterns. Migration strategy: - Provide a 'policy-migrate' CLI that takes legacy route documents and outputs suggestions + a --apply option. - For customers on Dedicated/Private, offer a migration runbook and opt-in migration assistance. Security & Compliance: - Plugin API will run in a sandboxed environment (separate FS, limited network) for Private deployments. - security_review_required: true

Console rejects uploads with fatal linter errors and surfaces repair guidance
CLI migration tool produces suggested patches and can apply safe fixes
Plugin sandboxing design documented and validated by security
Runtime startup fast-checks enabled with <5% cold-start overhead
